title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
authors: Piotr Białas, Christian D. Morales, Tomasz Stebel, Dawid Zapolski
abstract: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.
summary: This paper introduces a novel transformer-based neural network sampler for simulating the 2D XY model, a benchmark system in statistical mechanics. By incorporating physics knowledge like locality constraints and using advanced estimators like Neural Importance Sampling, the method achieves superior sampling efficiency compared to prior neural approaches. It provides a powerful, scalable tool for calculating thermodynamic properties in continuous spin systems.
main_problem: Developing efficient sampling methods for complex statistical physics systems to overcome the limitations of traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, such as critical slowing down.
main_result: A transformer-based variational autoregressive network significantly outperforms existing neural samplers, successfully reproducing key physical observables like energy and helicity modulus obtained via traditional MCMC.
method: The authors employ a variational approach using a transformer architecture to model the conditional probability density of the system's configuration, supplemented by Neural Importance Sampling (NIS) for asymptotically exact estimates.
model_or_system: The primary model is the two-dimensional XY model, which is used as a benchmark due to its continuous O(2) symmetry and its relevance to the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless (BKT) transition.
key_observables: Energy, magnetization, helicity modulus, and the partition function ($Z$), which is estimated via the NIS method.
important_parameters: Lattice size up to $96 	imes 96$, inverse temperature ($ eta$) near the BKT transition ($ eta \approx 1.12$).
main_assumptions: The variational estimate alone is insufficient; the NIS estimator is asymptotically exact provided the network covers the configuration space. Symmetrization techniques are used to improve sampling efficiency.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of Effective Sample Size (ESS) across different sampling techniques and the calculation of the Helicity modulus ($\Upsilon$) for various symmetry groups.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the neural sampler, details the transformer architecture with locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities, compares the variational estimate to the asymptotically exact NIS estimate, and discusses advanced techniques like lattice symmetry averaging to boost sampling quality.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the development of advanced, physics-informed neural samplers represents a powerful general methodology for simulating complex, high-dimensional quantum many-body systems where MCMC struggles.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic view of spin-by-spin configuration generation, for L = 6. Solid circles represent already generated spins, and the red spin (s21) is about to be generated. Locality-informed attention means that the conditional probability of a spin depends only on two rows of previously generated spins (darker circles). The approximate probabilities depend on two spins: top and left (for spin s21 this means s21,top = s15 and s21,left = s20).
